successCriteria.description: The LeaveType enum exposes exactly six string-valued members — ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY — and each member's runtime value equals its key name (e.g. LeaveType.ANNUAL === 'ANNUAL'). A reviewer can assert this by importing LeaveType and checking both the member set and individual values.

The LeaveRequestStatus enum exposes exactly five string-valued members — DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — and each member's runtime value equals its key name (e.g. LeaveRequestStatus.DRAFT === 'DRAFT'). A reviewer can assert this by importing LeaveRequestStatus and checking both the member set and individual values.

The BaseEntity interface is exported and, when an object is constructed with id (string), createdAt (Date), and updatedAt (Date), it satisfies the BaseEntity type without a TypeScript compile error. A reviewer can assert this by constructing such an object and confirming it is assignable to BaseEntity.

The Jest test file at tests/unit/shared/types/types.test.ts runs under the project's ts-jest configuration (testMatch **/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)) and passes with zero failures, verifying the enum member values and the BaseEntity interface shape. The verification command `npm run build && npx jest --passWithNoTests` exits zero.

The new source file compiles cleanly under the project's strict TypeScript configuration (tsc --noEmit, target ES2022, strict, baseUrl ./src) with no type errors, and the test file transforms cleanly under ts-jest at runtime.

constraints: The no-any rule from HARNESS.json constraints applies: use unknown with type guards instead of any. The type definitions and tests must not introduce any-typed values.

Follow the existing model style (uptime.model.ts, status.model.ts): plain exported interface and enum declarations directly in the module's public entry point. No classes, no decorators, no class-transformer/class-validator annotations, no extra runtime imports.

LeaveType and LeaveRequestStatus must be TypeScript string enums where each member's value equals its key name (e.g. ANNUAL = 'ANNUAL'). Numeric enums are not acceptable because the values persist to DB columns (leave_type, status on leave_requests) as strings.

The type definitions must live under src/shared/types/ (the architecture-declared owning location for BaseEntity, LeaveType, and LeaveRequestStatus). The test must live under tests/unit/shared/types/ to match jest.config.js testMatch. Do not place these cross-module shared types in a single-purpose module directory under src/modules/.

The shared-types module has zero upstream dependencies — it must not import from any other src module or external package. It is the foundation that five downstream modules (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit-log) depend on.
outOfScope: Employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, and audit-log modules are out of scope for this phase. Only the shared type definitions and their unit tests are delivered here.
No database migrations, repository implementations, or persistence-layer code are created in this phase. The types are pure compile-time definitions.
No changes to src/app.ts, src/index.ts, or any existing module's barrel index.ts. No route registration or service wiring. This phase only adds the shared types module and its test.

entityInvariants.invariant: BaseEntity is a pure data shape (no owned business logic) used by more than one module, so it must be defined in the shared-types module (src/shared/types/) and exported from that module's public entry point. It must remain a methodless interface — no behavior, no lifecycle methods — so downstream entities extend it as a structural contract only.

LeaveType is a cross-module value type (used by leave-policy, leave-balance, and leave-request) with no owned behavior, so it must be defined in the shared-types module and exported from its public entry point. Its member set is closed and fixed at the six declared values; no additional leave types may be added without an architecture change, because downstream policy and balance logic depends on the exact set.

LeaveRequestStatus is a cross-module value type (used by leave-request and audit-log) with no owned behavior, so it must be defined in the shared-types module and exported from its public entry point. Its member set is closed and fixed at the five declared lifecycle states (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED); the LeaveRequest lifecycle transitions defined in ARCHITECTURE.md depend on exactly these values, so no status may be added or removed without an architecture change.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Importing BaseEntity, LeaveType, and LeaveRequestStatus from the shared-types module's public entry point (src/shared/types/index.ts)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: N/A — pure type definitions, no runtime auth boundary
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: No runtime errors — these are compile-time type exports. A missing or misnamed export surfaces as a TypeScript compile error (tsc --noEmit fails), not a runtime exception.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The new type declarations must match the existing model style: plain `export interface` / `export enum` statements with no decorators, no classes, and no runtime imports. The existing uptime.model.ts and status.model.ts establish this convention.

If the shared-types module exposes its symbols via a barrel index.ts, it must follow the existing convention where index.ts re-exports the public symbols from the model file. The existing uptime/index.ts and status/index.ts establish this pattern. Since src/shared/types/index.ts is itself the module's public entry point, defining the types directly in it is also consistent.

The source file must compile under the project's tsconfig.json settings: strict mode (no implicit any, strict null checks), target ES2022, module commonjs, baseUrl ./src. The file is included by the "include": ["src"] glob and must not trigger any type errors under these settings.

The test file must be discoverable by jest.config.js: it must match the testMatch glob **/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js) and be transformable by the ts-jest preset. The test may import the source types via a bare import (shared/types) since moduleDirectories includes 'src', or via a relative path — both resolve correctly.

integrationPoints.target: Five downstream modules (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit-log) will import BaseEntity, LeaveType, and/or LeaveRequestStatus from src/shared/types/index.ts in subsequent phases. The exported symbol names and their types are the contract these phases depend on.
integrationPoints.why: The shared-types module is the foundation with zero upstream dependencies; all five domain modules depend on it. The exact exported names (BaseEntity, LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus) and their member sets must be stable so downstream phases can import them without modification.
